What We Do

Full-Service Otolaryngology (ENT) Revenue Cycle Management

Otolaryngology billing combines surgical CPT coding, in-office endoscopy and laryngoscopy billing, allergy testing and immunotherapy dose management, and hearing-related service coordination. PMEX reviews every operative and procedure report before coding and manages the full claim lifecycle.

ENT Surgical Coding

Sinus, tonsil, and laryngeal surgery CPT codes selected from the operative report.

Laryngoscopy Billing

Diagnostic and operative laryngoscopy (31505 to 31579) coded by procedure performed.

Allergy Testing and IT

Percutaneous testing and immunotherapy dose billing managed per visit.

Sinus Procedure Coding

FESS codes (31254 to 31297) billed per sinus opened and procedure performed.

Nasal Endoscopy Billing

Diagnostic nasal endoscopy (31231) and treatment codes billed separately from E/M.

Sleep Surgery Coding

UPPP, tonsillectomy, and septoplasty coded from the operative report.

Sound Familiar?

Common Otolaryngology (ENT) Billing Problems

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

FESS billed for fewer sinuses than were actually opened in the operative report.

PMEX reads every FESS operative report and codes each sinus opened with the correct CPT code per the documented procedure.

Diagnostic laryngoscopy bundled into the E/M instead of billed as a separate procedure.

PMEX submits diagnostic laryngoscopy with modifier 25 on the E/M when both are performed and separately documented.

Immunotherapy dose count wrong on multi-dose visits, underbilling by one or more doses.

PMEX counts administered doses from the injection log and bills 95115 or 95117 per the actual dose count on every visit.

UPPP or tonsillectomy denied for missing prior authorization from the commercial payer.

PMEX obtains surgical prior authorization before the OR date is confirmed for all elective ENT procedures.

Nasal endoscopy billed at the same time as a standard E/M without modifier 25.

PMEX applies modifier 25 to the E/M on every visit where a nasal endoscopy is separately performed and documented.

Biopsy taken during endoscopy not billed as a separate procedure.

PMEX reviews the endoscopy report for biopsy documentation and submits the biopsy code alongside the endoscopy on qualifying visits.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in Otolaryngology (ENT) Billing

ENT practices lose 15 to 24 percent of revenue to FESS under-coding, laryngoscopy bundling, and surgical authorization gaps.

PATTERN 01

FESS Under-Coded, Fewer Sinuses Billed Than Opened

Bilateral FESS with maxillary, ethmoid, and frontal sinuses opened. Billing team submits codes for maxillary and ethmoid only. Frontal sinus CPT code omitted. $280 per case in separately billable sinus procedure revenue not captured.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX reads every FESS operative report and codes each individual sinus opened with the correct HCPCS CPT code per the documented anatomy. Bilateral modifier 50 applied when procedures performed on both sides.

PATTERN 02

Laryngoscopy Denied as Bundled with E/M

Flexible diagnostic laryngoscopy (31575) performed during an office visit. Only the E/M submitted. Laryngoscopy not billed. Payer bundles it. $120 per encounter in diagnostic procedure revenue lost.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX submits the laryngoscopy code alongside the E/M with modifier 25 on every visit where the laryngoscopy is a separately documented diagnostic or therapeutic service beyond the scope of the office visit.

PATTERN 03

Elective ENT Surgery Denied, No Prior Authorization

Septoplasty and turbinate reduction scheduled. Commercial payer requires prior authorization. Case proceeds without confirmed auth. Surgeon and facility claims both denied. $1,400 professional fee denied retroactively.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX manages surgical prior authorization for all elective ENT procedures, confirming authorization is documented in the billing system before the OR date is placed on the schedule.
